title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 1 hour ago Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. For generations, it has been the biggest and richest source of employment in this major Ukrainian city. "Zaporizhstal is not just a big company, it's the heart of the city," he says. Now, following a series of Russian missile strikes, this heart has stopped beating. The huge factory that employs 8,500 people shut down indefinitely after four waves of Russian attacks - two in August, and two in September. "All the equipment has been almost completely destroyed. There are no windows left, and there are holes in the roofs. The blast furnaces have been almost completely ruined," Maksyshko complains. text: 🎥 28 сентября в кинозале Посольства России в Китае состоялся показ фильма «Чебурашка» (2023, реж. Дмитрий Дьяченко) для российских и китайских детей . Мероприятие посетили учащиеся школы при Посольстве , а также воспитанники средней школы Пекинского университета иностранных языков и школы столичного района Чаоян . Китайские друзья смогли не только познакомиться с современным прочтением истории Чебурашки — одного из самых узнаваемых и любимых героев отечественной мультипликации, но и пообщаться со своими российскими сверстниками . После просмотра для ребят было организовано чаепитие с угощениями . В рамках данного события диалог состоялся и между педагогами двух стран. Встреча прошла в теплой атмосфере, став еще одной возможностью для укрепления культурных связей и дружбы между подрастающими поколениями России и Китая.

title: Yekaterina Schulmann says Russian election expert Alexander Kynev’s leg was broken while he was being pressured to confess to treason
text: Political scientist Alexander Kynev, who was arrested on drug charges, had his leg broken by people demanding that he confess to treason, fellow political scientist Yekaterina Schulmann said on the September 29 episode of her show “Status.” “His leg really was broken in two places while he was being detained. That’s true, too. It’s also true that they used what had happened to his leg, along with electrical devices, to try to get him to confess to treason. He did not,” Schulmann said. Schulmann said the information had “come out” and was “now public knowledge, including internationally,” but did not say how she had learned of it. Kynev’s lawyer, Mikhail Biryukov, told the outlet Ekho that “the lawyers have no documents confirming what Schulmann said.” Kynev is one of the most respected experts on Russian regional politics and elections. On September 25, reports emerged that a court had ordered him held in custody on charges of producing and selling large quantities of drugs. The outlet Slovo Zashchite said Kynev was badly beaten while he was being detained. Я всю жизнь возлагал на него большие надежды, думал, увижу его генералом, отцом, поэтом, человеком, который поведёт за собой других. Он стал всем этим — только не успел состариться. Сынок, я хотел, чтобы ты был счастлив. Ты был счастлив в семье, в небе, в горах, в стихах, в службе. Ты выбрал десант, Рязань, Сирию, а потом и свой главный бой. Ты не сдался в окружении. Ты ушёл так, как подобает офицеру и мужчине. Для меня ты всегда был Героем, но прежде всего — мой сын. Я храню твои стихи, твои письма, твоё имя. Твоя дочь Теймия растёт, и мы с твоей женой Мадиной будем говорить ей, какой у неё был отец. Пока я жив, твоё имя будет звучать — везде, в нашей семье, в сердцах людей. Прости меня, если я был строг. text: Передовой рубеж противовоздушной обороны Операторы FPV-ПВО Центра "Рубикон" перехватили свыше 1500 дальнобойных БПЛА ВСУ, из них более половины - в сентябре 2026 года. В 2026 году противник сделал ставку на применение дальнобойных ударных БПЛА самолетного типа, бросив на реализацию этой угрозы миллиарды долларов . Сотни дальнобойных дронов противника ежедневно стремятся преодолеть рубежи ПВО и нанести ущерб тыловым объектам на территории Российской Федерации. Первыми на пути вражеских налетов встают операторы FPV-ПВО, перехватывающие значительную часть "дальнобойного залпа" противника, используя специализированные FPV-дроны. Специалисты Центра "Рубикон" успешно масштабировали наиболее эффективные способы борьбы с дальнобойными БПЛА противника, что подтверждается стремительным ростом количества перехватов данного типа целей. @lost_armour
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Эксклюзив «Военной хроники» : бойцы отряда «Шторм». Позывной Кипиш, часть 1. Был осужден на 15 лет колонии за разбой. Принял решение искупить свою вину перед Родиной и больше года назад ушел воевать на СВО. Во время штурма Родинского (ДНР) одним из первых заходил на шахты возле этого населенного пункта, помогал работать операторам дронов. Из-за тяжелой воздушной обстановки обеспечение передовых групп на шахтах получилось наладить не сразу. Первое время Кипиш сидел без воды, растапливая снег, а еду им сбрасывали с воздуха с помощью БПЛА «Молния». До того как зайти на шахты, активно участвовал в подвозах штурмовикам провизии, боекомплекта и медикаментов. Получил пять ранений. Был атакован дронами противника, подрывался на минах. «Я не сразу понял, куда попал. Понял только после первого ранения и когда люди вокруг начали гибнуть», – признается боец. Подробнее – в видео. Рекомендуем также посмотреть интервью командира «Штормов» с позывным Ногай — первая и вторая часть. источник
author: Boris Rozhin

title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 6 hours ago Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. For generations, it has been the biggest and richest source of employment in this major Ukrainian city. "Zaporizhstal is not just a big company, it's the heart of the city," he says. Now, following a series of Russian missile strikes, this heart has stopped beating. The huge factory that employs 8,500 people shut down indefinitely after four waves of Russian attacks - two in August, and two in September. "All the equipment has been almost completely destroyed. There are no windows left, and there are holes in the roofs. The blast furnaces have been almost completely ruined," Maksyshko complains. Russia fired a total of 17 missiles at Zaporizhstal, according to Oleksandr Myronenko, chief operating officer of steelworks owner Metinvest. Ei

text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. title: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries
text: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries Sep. 29, 2026 A Russian ruble faces off against U.S. dollars. Alexander Avilov / Moskva News Agency President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Tuesday tightening restrictions on taking cash from Russia to neighboring countries. Individuals are now prohibited from taking more than 1 million rubles ($11,900) in cash to Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are members of the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union. Individuals had previously been allowed to move the ruble equivalent of $100,000 under an order signed by Putin in March. In addition, businesses are banned from removing any amount of cash from the country , according to the newspaper Kommersant. Individual violators of the new restrictions face total confiscation of any sums exceeding 1 million rubles, while businesses caught attempting to transfer funds will be forced to surrender the entire cash amount. text: Putin Orders Russian Army to Increase Troop Size to 1.55M Sep. 29, 2026 Vladimir Putin looks to new horizons. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Monday that raises the strength of the Russian military by 15,500 troops, bringing the total number of active-duty servicemen to 1.55 million. Putin has raised the number of military personnel several times since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Monday’s order does not explain the reason for the latest increase. title: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14
text: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14 By Reuters Sep. 29, 2026 yarreg.ru Fourteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in the Yaroslavl region on Monday, state media reported, citing emergency services. One person was being treated for their injuries at the hospital. TASS reported that the fire had been put out. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Evrayev confirmed at least 10 deaths in a post on Telegram. He said first responders were still searching for potential other victims. The blaze engulfed two buildings in the village of Kubrinsk near the town of Pereslavl-Zalessky. Around 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene, Evrayev said. Law enforcement authorities launched a criminal investigation into possible industrial safety violations, TASS reported. title: Hundreds detained as student protests across France turn violent
text: 0:54 Students across France protest over poor school conditions - video France Hundreds detained as student protests across France turn violent More than 400 detained as police and students clash over class sizes, exhausting timetables and staff shortages Kim Willsher in Paris Tue 29 Sep 2026 19.27 EDT First published on Tue 29 Sep 2026 11.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google More than 400 people, most of them children, have been detained in France on Tuesday after teenagers across the country blockaded their schools in protest at class sizes, teacher shortages and long timetables. Interior minister Laurent Nunez told BFM TV: “440 were detained across national territory. We don’t have the final tally yet, but I’m told two-thirds led to police custody.” The education ministry said 400 schools were affected by protests or disruptions on Tuesday, out of about 3,700 across the country. The demonstrations began in Paris last week and have since escalated and spread across France. On Tuesday, high school pupils in Lille, northern France, set fire to dustbins and threw bottles, paving stones and other projectiles at police. Officers responded with teargas after protesters vandalised
author: Kim Willsher in Paris

text: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14 By Reuters Sep. 29, 2026 yarreg.ru Fourteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in the Yaroslavl region on Monday, state media reported, citing emergency services. One person was being treated for their injuries at the hospital. TASS reported that the fire had been put out. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Evrayev confirmed at least 10 deaths in a post on Telegram. He said first responders were still searching for potential other victims. The blaze engulfed two buildings in the village of Kubrinsk near the town of Pereslavl-Zalessky. Around 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene, Evrayev said. Law enforcement authorities launched a criminal investigation into possible industrial safety violations, TASS reported. text: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports Sep. 29, 2026 American rapper Ye performs in Istanbul, Turkey. Yasin Akgul / AFP Two St. Petersburg concerts by controversial rapper Ye scheduled for next month have been officially canceled following weeks of conflicting statements from venue management and local promoters. An Instagram account affiliated with the U.S. touring agency Access Opera confirmed the cancellation Tuesday, directing ticket holders to seek refunds from the Russian promoter Say Agency. The shows, originally scheduled for Oct. 10 and 11 at Gazprom Arena, triggered immediate backlash from conservative Russian politicians due to Ye’s past public support of Nazism, which constitutes a criminal offense under Russian law. Gazprom Arena claimed it had never signed a contract with Say Agency and could not host the Ye shows. title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 30 September 2026, 00:33 BST Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. For generations, it has been the biggest and richest source of employment in this major Ukrainian city. "Zaporizhstal is not just a big company, it's the heart of the city," he says. Now, following a series of Russian missile strikes, this heart has stopped beating. The huge factory that employs 8,500 people shut down indefinitely after four waves of Russian attacks - two in August, and two in September. "All the equipment has been almost completely destroyed. There are no windows left, and there are holes in the roofs. The blast furnaces have been almost completely ruined," Maksyshko complains. title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 30 September 2026 Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. title: Putin imposes new limits on taking cash rubles out of Russia
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has issued a decree barring people from taking more than 1 million rubles in cash from Russia to Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, or Uzbekistan. Under the decree, legal entities and sole proprietors cannot take cash to those countries, regardless of the amount, though there are stated exceptions. The restrictions do not apply to cash that legal entities carry in transit or to rubles taken abroad to support Russian diplomatic missions. In other cases, cash may be taken out through airports the government will designate. The person carrying it must have a bank statement showing that the money was withdrawn from their own accounts. Cash taken out in violation of the ban will be seized: the full amount from legal entities and sole proprietors, and any amount above the 1 million ruble limit from individuals. The new decree tightens restrictions on taking cash and gold out of Russia that Putin introduced in April 2026. That decree barred people from taking more than $100,000 worth of rubles in cash to countries in the Eurasian Economic Union . It also barred them from taking refined gold bars weighing a total of 100 grams

title: Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk to close two of its five maternity hospitals after regional birth rate nearly halves
text: Two of Krasnoyarsk’s five maternity hospitals, Nos. 4 and 6, will close at the end of 2026. That will leave Leninsky District without a maternity hospital and reduce the number in Sovetsky District from two to one. Staff at both hospitals oppose the closures and have called on Moscow to intervene. The Krasnoyarsk regional Health Ministry cited a falling birth rate and insisted the closures would not cause a shortage of beds. According to the ministry, births in the region fell by nearly half, from 44,000 in 2014 to 23,000 in 2025. “The city’s maternity hospitals now have several times the capacity needed to meet actual demand,” said Alexey Konovalenko, the Krasnoyarsk region’s health minister. Staff at the hospitals facing closure disagree. They have recorded two appeals to Vladimir Putin. Medical workers at Maternity Hospital No. 4, which is slated for closure, complained that management suggested they look for jobs in other cities or retrain for a new profession and threatened to put those who objected on “blacklists.” “If you fall out of favor with a chief doctor, and then with the Health Ministry, you won’t be able to find another job in medicine,” staff members said. title: The Atlantic: Trump backs plan to ease Russia sanctions in exchange for political prisoners without waiting for the Ukraine war to end
text: U.S. President Donald Trump has approved a proposal to ease sanctions on Russia in exchange for the release of political prisoners, The Atlantic reports. According to the magazine’s Simon Shuster, special envoy John Coale proposed the approach. Coale secured the release of about 500 political prisoners in Belarus in exchange for sanctions relief. Washington and Minsk have also begun discussing a major deal to buy Belarusian potash, as Trump announced last week. Coale says Russia is involved in the talks because European sanctions mean Belarusian potash will have to be exported through Russia. Coale’s plan for Moscow is still in its early stages and aims to break the deadlock in talks between Russia and the United States, Shuster says. In Shuster’s view, it would give Vladimir Putin an easy way to show goodwill and signs of diplomatic progress with the United States without stopping Russia’s strikes on Ukraine. In exchange for the release of prisoners, Washington could offer the Kremlin sanctions relief and a return to trade deals. title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 30 September 2026 Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. For generations, it has been the biggest and richest source of employment in this major Ukrainian city. "Zaporizhstal is not just a big company, it's the heart of the city," he says. Now, following a series of Russian missile strikes, this heart has stopped beating. The huge factory that employs 8,500 people shut down indefinitely after four waves of Russian attacks - two in August, and two in September. "All the equipment has been almost completely destroyed. There are no windows left, and there are holes in the roofs. The blast furnaces have been almost completely ruined," Maksyshko complains. Russia fired a total of 17 missiles at Zaporizhstal, according to Oleksandr Myronenko, chief operating officer of steelworks owner Metinve

title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

Individuals are now prohibited from taking more than 1 million rubles ($11,900) in cash to Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are members of the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union. title: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14
text: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14 By Reuters Sep. 29, 2026 yarreg.ru Fourteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in the Yaroslavl region on Monday, state media reported, citing emergency services. One person was being treated for their injuries at the hospital. TASS reported that the fire had been put out. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Evrayev confirmed at least 10 deaths in a post on Telegram. He said first responders were still searching for potential other victims. The blaze engulfed two buildings in the village of Kubrinsk near the town of Pereslavl-Zalessky. Around 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene, Evrayev said. Law enforcement authorities launched a criminal investigation into possible industrial safety violations, TASS reported. title: 'Putin's goal is to prolong his power in Russia': Journalist Roman Badanin
text: 'Putin's goal is to prolong his power in Russia': Journalist Roman Badanin Europe To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. Try again Cover image: PERSPECTIVE © FRANCE 24 09:54 Issued on: 29/09/2026 - 14:46 09:54 min Share From the show Reading time 1 min A journalist who has spent more than 20 years investigating Russian leader Vladimir Putin and who is recognised as perhaps Russia's finest investigative journalist has told FRANCE 24 that Putin's aim with the war in Ukraine is simply to prolong his power inside Russia. Roman Badanin has just published a book, "Le Tsar en personne" or "The Tsar in person" which delves into exactly how Putin's mind works. Badanin says Putin acts like a gang member, and his attitude is that "if you beat me, I will beat you even harder". The book is so far out in Russian and French, with an English version to follow. title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
text: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign Image source, Metinvest/Zaporizhstal Image caption, After one attack on the Zaporizhzhia steelworks, a blast furnace was restarted only for the site to be hit again hours later By Vitaly Shevchenko Chief Analyst, BBC Monitoring Published 30 September 2026 Like thousands of other residents of Zaporizhzhia, Denys Maksyshko has spent years working for local steel factory Zaporizhstal. text: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports Sep. 29, 2026 American rapper Ye performs in Istanbul, Turkey. Yasin Akgul / AFP Two St. Petersburg concerts by controversial rapper Ye scheduled for next month have been officially canceled following weeks of conflicting statements from venue management and local promoters. An Instagram account affiliated with the U.S. touring agency Access Opera confirmed the cancellation Tuesday, directing ticket holders to seek refunds from the Russian promoter Say Agency. The shows, originally scheduled for Oct. 10 and 11 at Gazprom Arena, triggered immediate backlash from conservative Russian politicians due to Ye’s past public support of Nazism, which constitutes a criminal offense under Russian law. Gazprom Arena claimed it had never signed a contract with Say Agency and could not host the Ye shows. title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

Sputnik / Gavriil Grigorov / Pool via REUTERS Russian President Vladimir Putin's special envoy Kirill Dmitriev held "constructive" talks with U.S. officials on ending the Ukraine war, including possible U.S.-Russia energy initiatives in the postwar period, a U.S. official said on Tuesday. The visit Monday by Dmitriev, who is also head of Russia's RDIF sovereign wealth fund, follows a meeting between President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last week in New York, where Zelensky said they discussed a potential ceasefire on energy-related targets. news Putin Envoy Kirill Dmitriev Meets With Witkoff and Kushner to Discuss Russian Energy Read more Trump special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Putin in Moscow earlier this month. Dmitriev was in Washington "to continue constructive discussions on a peaceful resolution to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and possible U.S.-Russia energy initiatives after the war ends," the U.S. official said. title: Kremlin Denies Orchestrating Arson Attack at Estonian Robotics Plant
text: Kremlin Denies Orchestrating Arson Attack at Estonian Robotics Plant Sep. 29, 2026 A Milrem Robotics booth at an exhibition in London. Milrem Robotics The Kremlin has denied accusations that it was behind a fire that broke out at a military robotics plant in Estonia last month. Estonia’s Internal Security Service (KAPO) claimed Tuesday that Russia orchestrated an Aug. 15 arson attack against Milrem Robotics, which supplies unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine “The modus operandi of the Milrem attack is consistent with other acts of sabotage carried out in Europe on behalf of Russia,” KAPO said in a statement, adding that “these activities are intended to undermine support for Ukraine.” Estonia did not disclose its evidence in the case, citing the confidentiality of security services, but said the incident “demonstrates the continued need for industries… to maintain robust physical and cyber security measures.” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later told reporters that Estonia’s accusations were false. “Such statements are baseless, ill-considered, bear no relation whatsoever to reality and lack any form of reasoning. Consequently, we cannot and will not take such statements seriously

title: Putin Orders Russian Army to Increase Troop Size to 1.55M
text: Putin Orders Russian Army to Increase Troop Size to 1.55M Sep. 29, 2026 Vladimir Putin looks to new horizons. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Monday that raises the strength of the Russian military by 15,500 troops, bringing the total number of active-duty servicemen to 1.55 million. Putin has raised the number of military personnel several times since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Monday’s order does not explain the reason for the latest increase. title: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14
text: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14 By Reuters Sep. 29, 2026 yarreg.ru Fourteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in the Yaroslavl region on Monday, state media reported, citing emergency services. One person was being treated for their injuries at the hospital. TASS reported that the fire had been put out. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Evrayev confirmed at least 10 deaths in a post on Telegram. He said first responders were still searching for potential other victims. The blaze engulfed two buildings in the village of Kubrinsk near the town of Pereslavl-Zalessky. Around 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene, Evrayev said. Law enforcement authorities launched a criminal investigation into possible industrial safety violations, TASS reported. title: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports
text: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports Sep. 29, 2026 American rapper Ye performs in Istanbul, Turkey. Yasin Akgul / AFP Two St. Petersburg concerts by controversial rapper Ye scheduled for next month have been officially canceled following weeks of conflicting statements from venue management and local promoters. An Instagram account affiliated with the U.S. touring agency Access Opera confirmed the cancellation Tuesday, directing ticket holders to seek refunds from the Russian promoter Say Agency. The shows, originally scheduled for Oct. 10 and 11 at Gazprom Arena, triggered immediate backlash from conservative Russian politicians due to Ye’s past public support of Nazism, which constitutes a criminal offense under Russian law. Gazprom Arena claimed it had never signed a contract with Say Agency and could not host the Ye shows. Local media reported at the time that the sudden cancellation followed a phone call “from above,” suggesting the Kremlin may have directly intervened. title: Ksenia Maximova Went From Top Model to Anti-War Activist to London Councillor. Now She’s Wanted By Russia.
text: Ksenia Maximova Went From Top Model to Anti-War Activist to London Councillor. Now She’s Wanted By Russia. By Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 29, 2026 Ksenia Maximova. Courtesy photo Ksenia Maximova was ranked among the world’s 50 most successful models in the 2000s, but today is better known as a prominent figure in Russia’s anti-war movement in London. Since 2022, Maximova has worked to support Ukraine, help anti-war Russian emigres and refugees in Britain and collaborated with the Russian Anti-War Committee. More recently, she became a rare Russian-born figure to enter British politics after she was elected as a Liberal Democrat councillor in London. On Monday, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) opened a criminal case against her, accusing her of participating in a “terrorist organization” and claiming that the Russian Democratic Society, which she co-founded, collected money and other assistance “in the interests of the Kyiv regime.” Maximova, 40, was also placed on Russia’s wanted list and added to its register of “terrorists and extremists.” In an interview with The Moscow Times, Maximova discussed entering British politics as a Russian immigrant, her work supporting Ukraine

title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

title: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries
text: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries Sep. 29, 2026 A Russian ruble faces off against U.S. dollars. Alexander Avilov / Moskva News Agency President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Tuesday tightening restrictions on taking cash from Russia to neighboring countries. Individuals are now prohibited from taking more than 1 million rubles ($11,900) in cash to Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are members of the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union. Individuals had previously been allowed to move the ruble equivalent of $100,000 under an order signed by Putin in March. In addition, businesses are banned from removing any amount of cash from the country , according to the newspaper Kommersant. news Kremlin Seizes Russian Subsidiary of German Retailer Metro Read more Individual violators of the new restrictions face total confiscation of any sums exceeding 1 million rubles, while businesses caught attempting to transfer funds will be forced to surrender the entire cash amount. title: Russian Summer Air Travel Fell Amid Surge in Daily Drone Attacks
text: Russian Summer Air Travel Fell Amid Surge in Daily Drone Attacks Sep. 29, 2026 Passengers at Moscow’s Sheremetyevo Airport. Alexander Avilov / Moskva News Agency Russian airlines recorded a 7% drop in passenger traffic during the summer travel season, as a surge of daily Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted operations at dozens of airports across the country, the Interfax news agency reported Tuesday. Dmitry Yadrov, who heads the civilian aviation agency Rosaviatsia, said in a meeting with Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin that Russian airlines transported 39.5 million passengers between May and August. That is reportedly down from around 42.6 million passengers who were transported over the same period last year. title: 'Putin's goal is to prolong his power in Russia': Journalist Roman Badanin
text: 'Putin's goal is to prolong his power in Russia': Journalist Roman Badanin Europe To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. Accept Manage my choices One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Try again Cover image: PERSPECTIVE © FRANCE 24 09:54 Issued on: 29/09/2026 - 14:46 09:54 min Share From the show Reading time 1 min A journalist who has spent more than 20 years investigating Russian leader Vladimir Putin and who is recognised as perhaps Russia's finest investigative journalist has told FRANCE 24 that Putin's aim with the war in Ukraine is simply to prolong his power inside Russia. Roman Badanin has just published a book, "Le Tsar en personne" or "The Tsar in person" which delves into exactly how Putin's mind works. Badanin says Putin acts like a gang member, and his attitude is that "if you beat me, I will beat you even harder". The book is so far out in Russian and French, with an English version to follow. He spoke to us in Perspective. By: Stuart Norval Video by: Stuart Norval On the same topic Hybrid warfare:

text: News , People – September 29, 2026 Senior Leadership Changes In The 1st Azov Corps Photo: 1st Azov Corps, September 26, 2026. David Pipe Share: In the last month and a half, following the establishment of the new Operation Task Force “Azov” , several changes have occurred within the senior leadership of the 1st Azov Corps , as well as the Azov Brigade. On September 25, 2026, MilitaryLand reported on the change of leadership within the 12th Special Purpose Brigade “Azov” , with Lieutenant Colonel Lev Pashko, callsign “Khorus”, assuming command of the brigade, becoming one of the youngest and most highly regarded commanders in the history of the unit. Read also Pashko Takes Command of the Azov Brigade The appointment, however, represents only the latest in a series of changes to the senior leadership of Azov, extending from the brigade to the 1st Azov Corps and the newly established Operation Task Force “Azov” Changes within the Azov Brigade Pashko succeeded Lieutenant Colonel Bohdan Hryshenkov, callsign “Puhach”, who had commanded the Azov Brigade since April 2025, following the establishment of the 1st Azov Corps. text: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports Sep. 29, 2026 American rapper Ye performs in Istanbul, Turkey. Yasin Akgul / AFP Two St. Petersburg concerts by controversial rapper Ye scheduled for next month have been officially canceled following weeks of conflicting statements from venue management and local promoters. An Instagram account affiliated with the U.S. touring agency Access Opera confirmed the cancellation Tuesday, directing ticket holders to seek refunds from the Russian promoter Say Agency. title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

Courtesy photo Ksenia Maximova was ranked among the world’s 50 most successful models in the 2000s, but today is better known as a prominent figure in Russia’s anti-war movement in London. Since 2022, Maximova has worked to support Ukraine, help anti-war Russian emigres and refugees in Britain and collaborated with the Russian Anti-War Committee. More recently, she became a rare Russian-born figure to enter British politics after she was elected as a Liberal Democrat councillor in London. On Monday, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) opened a criminal case against her, accusing her of participating in a “terrorist organization” and claiming that the Russian Democratic Society, which she co-founded, collected money and other assistance “in the interests of the Kyiv regime.” Maximova, 40, was also placed on Russia’s wanted list and added to its register of “terrorists and extremists.” In an interview with The Moscow Times, Maximova discussed entering British politics as a Russian immigrant, her work supporting Ukraine

title: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region
text: At Least 6 Crew Members Confirmed Dead After Military Plane Crashes in Amur Region Sep. 29, 2026 Social media Six crew members on board a Russian military aircraft that crashed in the Far Eastern Amur region were killed, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The Tu-95 strategic bomber went down in a remote area during a routine training exercise, the Interfax news agency cited a military spokesperson as saying. It was not carrying any weapons on board at the time of the crash. One crew member survived the crash and was hospitalized, the Defense Ministry said. Air Force officials were dispatched to the crash site to conduct an investigation. Unverified reports from Telegram news with ties to Russian law enforcement and security services claimed the bomber plane may have crashed as the result of an engine fire and explosion. Officials have not commented on the possible cause of the crash. The Tu-95 was reportedly stationed at the Ukrainka air base, one of Russia’s largest long-range Air Force bases. Reports said the plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo, which is located 30 kilometers (18.5 miles) north of the Ukrainka base. Read more about: Aircrash , Air Force , Amur reg

title: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries
text: Russia Tightens Cash Outflow Limits to Neighboring Countries Sep. 29, 2026 A Russian ruble faces off against U.S. dollars. Alexander Avilov / Moskva News Agency President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Tuesday tightening restrictions on taking cash from Russia to neighboring countries. Individuals are now prohibited from taking more than 1 million rubles ($11,900) in cash to Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are members of the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union. Individuals had previously been allowed to move the ruble equivalent of $100,000 under an order signed by Putin in March. title: Kremlin Denies Orchestrating Arson Attack at Estonian Robotics Plant
text: Kremlin Denies Orchestrating Arson Attack at Estonian Robotics Plant Sep. 29, 2026 A Milrem Robotics booth at an exhibition in London. Milrem Robotics The Kremlin has denied accusations that it was behind a fire that broke out at a military robotics plant in Estonia last month. Estonia’s Internal Security Service (KAPO) claimed Tuesday that Russia orchestrated an Aug. 15 arson attack against Milrem Robotics, which supplies unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine “The modus operandi of the Milrem attack is consistent with other acts of sabotage carried out in Europe on behalf of Russia,” KAPO said in a statement, adding that “these activities are intended to undermine support for Ukraine.” Estonia did not disclose its evidence in the case, citing the confidentiality of security services, but said the incident “demonstrates the continued need for industries… to maintain robust physical and cyber security measures.” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later told reporters that Estonia’s accusations were false. “Such statements are baseless, ill-considered, bear no relation whatsoever to reality and lack any form of reasoning. text: Putin Orders Russian Army to Increase Troop Size to 1.55M Sep. 29, 2026 Vladimir Putin looks to new horizons. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order on Monday that raises the strength of the Russian military by 15,500 troops, bringing the total number of active-duty servicemen to 1.55 million. title: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14
text: Fire at Pyrotechnics Factory in Yaroslavl Region Kills 14 By Reuters Sep. 29, 2026 yarreg.ru Fourteen people were killed in a fire at a pyrotechnics factory in the Yaroslavl region on Monday, state media reported, citing emergency services. One person was being treated for their injuries at the hospital. TASS reported that the fire had been put out. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Evrayev confirmed at least 10 deaths in a post on Telegram. He said first responders were still searching for potential other victims. The blaze engulfed two buildings in the village of Kubrinsk near the town of Pereslavl-Zalessky. Around 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene, Evrayev said. Law enforcement authorities launched a criminal investigation into possible industrial safety violations, TASS reported. title: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports
text: Ye Shows in St. Petersburg Officially Canceled After Weeks of Conflicting Reports Sep. 29, 2026 American rapper Ye performs in Istanbul, Turkey. Yasin Akgul / AFP Two St. Petersburg concerts by controversial rapper Ye scheduled for next month have been officially canceled following weeks of conflicting statements from venue management and local promoters. An Instagram account affiliated with the U.S. touring agency Access Opera confirmed the cancellation Tuesday, directing ticket holders to seek refunds from the Russian promoter Say Agency. The shows, originally scheduled for Oct. 10 and 11 at Gazprom Arena, triggered immediate backlash from conservative Russian politicians due to Ye’s past public support of Nazism, which constitutes a criminal offense under Russian law. Gazprom Arena claimed it had never signed a contract with Say Agency and could not host the Ye shows. Local media reported at the time that the sudden cancellation followed a phone call “from above,” suggesting the Kremlin may have directly intervened. Read also Pashko Takes Command of the Azov Brigade The appointment, however, represents only the latest in a series of changes to the senior leadership of Azov, extending from the brigade to the 1st Azov Corps and the newly established Operation Task Force “Azov” Changes within the Azov Brigade Pashko succeeded Lieutenant Colonel Bohdan Hryshenkov, callsign “Puhach”, who had commanded the Azov Brigade since April 2025, following the establishment of the 1st Azov Corps.
